A.explanation: Amplitude is the peak height of the trace and needs a vertical distance with the volts per division setting, not a horizontal distance.

B.explanation: A horizontal length of one cycle with the time-base setting gives period $T$, then $f = 1/T$ gives the sound frequency.

C.explanation: Speed needs $v = f\lambda$, so frequency from the CRO alone is not enough without wavelength or distance information.

D.explanation: Wavelength is a distance in space in $\text{m}$, but the CRO horizontal axis shows time, so it cannot give $\lambda$ directly.

hints: Notice the question allows only a horizontal distance on the sine trace, which runs left to right along the time direction, not the up-down voltage direction.
Recall the CRO time-base control in $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ or $\text{s div}^{-1}$ converts a horizontal length of one complete cycle into the period $T$.
Use $f = 1/T$ to link that period to a sound-wave property, and ask why speed and wavelength would also need a length in air.
walkthrough: On the CRO the vertical deflection shows microphone voltage and the horizontal deflection shows time, so a horizontal distance measures a time interval.
Measure the horizontal length of one full sine wave on the screen, for example the distance from one peak to the next peak.
Multiply that length in $\text{cm}$ or divisions by the time-base setting in $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ to get the period $T$ in $\text{s}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ to calculate the frequency in $\text{Hz}$, which is the frequency of the microphone voltage and of the sound wave.
Amplitude would need vertical height, and speed and wavelength would need a spatial measurement, so only frequency follows from time alone. This is option B.
